feature: Implement a bespoke numeric mini-language interpreter and expose it as Math.run(src: string): string. The subsystem lives in new files under Runtime/MiniLang/; registration is a single Math method (Math is 'any', so no TypeSystem change is needed).
implementation: Lexer: tokenizes numbers (int/decimal), identifiers, the keywords let/print, operators + - * / = ( ), and treats newline or ';' as a statement separator; whitespace is otherwise ignored.

Parser: recursive-descent. program := stmt (SEP stmt)*; stmt := 'let' IDENT '=' expr | 'print' expr; expr := term (('+'|'-') term)*; term := factor (('*'|'/') factor)*; factor := '-' factor | primary; primary := NUMBER | IDENT | '(' expr ')'. This yields standard precedence and left-associativity.
MlValue: a struct holding a double (Number kind only in stage 1). Display() formats like JS: integer-valued -> no decimal (via double.ToString("R")), -0 collapses to 0.
Environment: flat Dictionary<string, MlValue>; Get throws MlError("undefined variable '<name>'") on a miss.
Interpreter.Run(src): lex -> parse -> execute, joining print lines with '\n' (no trailing newline). Any MlError is caught and returned as the single line 'error: <message>'.
MathBuiltIns.cs: register .MethodV2("run", 1, ...) returning RuntimeValue.FromString(Interpreter.Run(args[0].AsString())). Math is 'any' at the type level so no static signature is required.
stage_split_rationale: Stage 1 establishes the whole numeric interpreter skeleton across ~9 files (lexer, parser, AST, values, environment, evaluator, errors, plus the Math.run registration). Stage 2 adds a string type, which by design must thread through nearly every one of those files (token type, lexer string scanning, AST string/call nodes, parser, value union, evaluator + overload) - the cross-cutting integration that defeats weaker models.
key_traps: The SharpTS.csproj uses the default SDK compile glob (no EnableDefaultCompileItems=false), so new .cs files under Runtime/MiniLang/ are picked up automatically with NO csproj change. A stale obj/ cache can mask new files; a clean build resolves it.
Math.run must return a STRING (RuntimeValue.FromString), not a number - the printed program output is text.
Integer-valued doubles must print without a decimal point (JS semantics); double.ToString("R") on an integer-valued double already produces no decimal.
Output joins print lines with a single newline and has NO trailing newline; the hidden driver compares trimmed stdout from console.log.
baseline_behavior: On pristine source Math.run does not exist; calling it prints a runtime TypeError line (exit 0) instead of the program output, so every exact-match hidden check fails.
expected_failure_summary: Baseline (feature absent): 0/14 hidden checks pass. Accepted (reference impl applied to pristine): 14/14 pass.
